You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

m = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC: mark compartments containing repeated anomaly cells', content='For ARC grids partitioned by full-width horizontal divider rows and full-height vertical divider columns, treat each resulting equal-sized compartment as one output cell when demonstrations support it. If a compartment is mostly a uniform background color with isolated cells of another color, count the isolated anomaly cells in each compartment. The demonstrated rule here outputs a compact matrix with one cell per compartment: use the original background color as the output background, and place marker color 1 at the position of any compartment containing exactly two anomaly cells; compartments with zero or one anomaly stay background. Demonstration: a 19x11 grid had four 4x2 compartment rows and four 2-wide compartment columns (separators color 5); anomalous color 0 appeared in each block, and only block (row-band 1, column-block 3) had two anomalies, so output was 4x4 of color 2 with a 1 at output [1][3]. In the solved 19x5 test, separators color 3 made four bands and two columns; color 5 occurred twice in blocks [1][1] and [2][1], yielding a 4x2 output with those two cells marked 1 and all others background 7. Infer marker/count rule from demos rather than assuming the threshold for new tasks.', global_=True)
print(m)
